341842.title: The first partial theta Borwein conjecture
341842.statement:
Let $m$ and $k$ be non-negative integers. For $n$ a non-negative integer, write $(a;q)_n:=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-aq^j)$ and $(a_1,\dots,a_m;q)_n:=\prod_{r=1}^m(a_r;q)_n$. Define Laurent polynomials $A_{m,n,k}(q)$, $B_{m,n,k}(q)$, and $C_{m,n,k}(q)$ by

$$
(q,q^2;q^3)_n\prod_{j=1}^m(p^jq,p^jq^2;q^3)_n(p^jq^{-1},p^jq^{-2};q^{-3})_n
=\sum_{k\geq0}p^k\left[A_{m,n,k}(q^3)-qB_{m,n,k}(q^3)-q^2C_{m,n,k}(q^3)\right].
$$

**The first partial theta Borwein conjecture.** For each $m,k\geq0$, there is a non-negative integer $N_{m,k}$ such that, if $n\geq N_{m,k}$, then $A_{m,n,k}(q)$, $B_{m,n,k}(q)$, and $C_{m,n,k}(q)$ have non-negative coefficients. Moreover, for $m=1$, $N_{1,k}=0$ for $k\leq4$ and $N_{1,k}=\lceil k/4\rceil$ for $k\geq5$; for $m>1$, $N_{m,k}=N_k$ is independent of $m$.

This is a partial-theta extension of Borwein's first conjecture, whose corresponding positivity statement was settled by Wang. The displayed values of $N_{m,k}$ are computationally supported, while the asserted eventual coefficient non-negativity remains conjectural.
341842.source_name: Gaurav Bhatnagar and Michael J. Schlosser, “A partial theta function Borwein conjecture”, arXiv:1902.04447 (2019).
341842.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

341843.title: The generalized partial theta Borwein conjecture
341843.statement:
Let $m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,$ and $k$ be non-negative integers. Define Laurent polynomials $A(q)=A_{m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,k}(q)$, $B(q)=B_{m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,k}(q)$, and $C(q)=C_{m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,k}(q)$ by

$$
(q,q^2;q^3)_{n_1}\prod_{j=1}^{m_1}(p^jq,p^jq^2;q^3)_{n_2}\prod_{j=1}^{m_2}(p^jq^{-1},p^jq^{-2};q^{-3})_{n_3}
=\sum_{k\geq0}p^k\left[A(q^3)-qB(q^3)-q^2C(q^3)\right].
$$

**The generalized partial theta Borwein conjecture.** For fixed $k$, if $m_1,m_2\geq1$ and $n_1,n_2,n_3$ are sufficiently large, then $A(q)$, $B(q)$, and $C(q)$ have non-negative coefficients.

This conjecture extends the first partial-theta Borwein conjecture by allowing the positive and negative $q$-shifted-factorial truncations to have separate parameters. The source gives no proof or resolution, and its formulation contains a duplicated “if,” so the intended quantifier structure should be checked against the published version.
341843.source_name: Gaurav Bhatnagar and Michael J. Schlosser, “A partial theta function Borwein conjecture”, arXiv:1902.04447 (2019).
341843.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

341844.title: The generalized odd-modulus partial theta Borwein conjecture
341844.statement:
Let $m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,$ and $k$ be non-negative integers, and let $K$ be a positive number. Define $A_k(q)=A_{m_1,m_2,n_1,n_2,n_3,k,K}(q)$ by

$$
(q^K,q^{K+1};q^{2K+1})_{n_1}\prod_{j=1}^{m_1}(p^jq^K,p^jq^{K+1};q^{2K+1})_{n_2}\prod_{j=1}^{m_2}(p^jq^{-K},p^jq^{-K-1};q^{-2K-1})_{n_3}=\sum_{k\geq0}p^kA_k(q),
$$

where $A_k(q)=\sum_Ma_{M,k}q^M$, and let $l=\left\lfloor(2K+1)/4\right\rfloor$.

**The generalized odd-modulus partial theta Borwein conjecture.** For fixed $k$ and $K$, if $m_1,m_2\geq1$ and $n_1,n_2,n_3$ are sufficiently large, then

$$
a_{M,k}\geq0\quad\text{if }M\equiv0,\pm i\pmod{2K+1}\text{ for some }i\in\{1,2,\dots,l\},
$$

and $a_{M,k}\leq0$ otherwise.

This extends the Borwein sign pattern to truncated theta products with odd modulus $2K+1$. The source presents it as a conjectural pattern supported by computation; no resolution is supplied.
341844.source_name: Gaurav Bhatnagar and Michael J. Schlosser, “A partial theta function Borwein conjecture”, arXiv:1902.04447 (2019).
341844.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

342364.title: The 2-adic valuation conjecture for even-colored 2-ary partition functions
342364.statement:
Let $c_m(n)$ denote the $m$-colored binary partition function, and let $
u_2$ be the 2-adic valuation. For positive integers $k,n$ and nonnegative integers $k$ as specified below, consider the differences of the values of $c_m$. **2-adic valuation conjecture.** For $kin\mathbb{N}_{+}$ and each $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{2k}(4n)-c_{2k}(n))=\nu_{2}(n)+2\nu_{2}(k)+3.
$$
 Moreover, for $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$, 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+1}(4n)-c_{4k+1}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+3,
$$
 
$$
\nu_{2}(c_{4k+3}(4n)-c_{4k+3}(n))\geq\nu_{2}(n)+6.
$$
 In each case, equality holds for infinitely many $n\in\mathbb{N}$. These predictions are motivated by known sharp congruences for the ordinary binary partition function and numerical computations for $m\leq10$ and $n\leq10^5$; their general validity remains open.
342364.source_name: Maciej Ulas and Błażej Żmija, “On p-adic valuations of certain m colored p-ary partition functions”, arXiv:1904.03398 (2019).
342364.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.03398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

343330.title: Finite vertical-strip expansion formula for shifted stable Grothendieck polynomials
343330.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a strict partition. For strict partitions $\lambda\supseteq\mu$ with $\ell(\lambda)=\ell(\mu)$, let $\textsf{SD}_{\lambda/\mu}$ be the shifted skew diagram. A **vertical strip** is a subset of $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\times\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ containing at most one position in each row, and let $c(\lambda/\mu)$ be the number of distinct columns occupied by positions in $\textsf{SD}_{\lambda/\mu}$. **Vertical-strip expansion conjecture.** Then

$$
G\hspace{-0.2mm}Q^{(\beta)}_\mu=2^{\ell(\mu)}\cdot\sum_{\lambda}(-1)^{c(\lambda/\mu)}\cdot(-\beta/2)^{|\lambda/\mu|}\cdot G\hspace{-0.2mm}P^{(\beta)}_\lambda,
$$

where the sum is over the finite set of such strict partitions $\lambda$ for which $\textsf{SD}_{\lambda/\mu}$ is a vertical strip. The source reports that computer calculations suggest this finite formula and gives it as the ensuing conjectural description of the expansion.
343330.source_name: Joel Brewster Lewis and Eric Marberg, “Enriched set-valued P-partitions and shifted stable Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:1907.10691 (2020).
343330.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.10691

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

345183.title: Non-holonomicity conjecture for the two-player winning probability
345183.statement:
Let $p=q=1/2$, and let $W_{n,0,0}(x)$ be the probability generating function for the two-player pile game with boundary, with $n$ the initial pile size. Define the first player's winning probability by

$$
\bar{w}(n):=W_{n,0,0}(1).
$$

A sequence is **holonomic** if it satisfies a linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients. **Non-holonomicity conjecture.** The winning probability sequence $\bar{w}(n)$ is not holonomic: there are no specific $N$ and polynomials $p_0(n),p_1(n),\dots,p_N(n)$ such that

$$
p_0(n)\bar{w}(n)+p_1(n)\bar{w}(n-1)+\dots+p_N(n)\bar{w}(n-N)=0.
$$

The conjecture concerns the apparent absence of a linear recurrence for the two-player winning probabilities, in contrast with related pile games where the corresponding sequence is holonomic of small order. The evidence presented is computational and the conjecture remains open.
345183.source_name: Ho-Hon Leung and Thotsaporn "Aek'' Thanatipanonda, “Game of Pure Chance with Restricted Boundary”, arXiv:2001.05108 (2020).
345183.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

345966.title: Fu and Lin's four-statistic equidistribution conjecture for 2314-avoiding permutations
345966.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ be the permutations avoiding the vincular pattern $\underline{23}14$, and let $cmathbf{I}_n(110)$ be the inversion sequences avoiding $110$. For a permutation $cmathit{\pi}$, let $cmathrm{rmin}$, $cmathrm{lmin}$ and $cmathrm{rmax}$ denote the numbers of right-to-left minima, left-to-right minima and right-to-left maxima, respectively, and let $cmathrm{asc}$ denote the number of ascents. For an inversion sequence $e$, let $cmathrm{zero}(e)$ be the number of zero entries, $cmathrm{max}(e)=|\{i\in[n]:e_i=i-1\}|$, and $cmathrm{rep}(e)=n-|\{e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n\}|$.
**Fu and Lin's equidistribution conjecture.** The quadruple $(\operatorname{rmin},\operatorname{lmin},\operatorname{rmax},\operatorname{asc})$ on $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ has the same distribution as $(\operatorname{zero},\operatorname{max},\operatorname{rmin},\operatorname{rep})$ on $cmathbf{I}_n(110)$.
The conjecture was verified computationally for $1\leq n\leq9$ and refines the proposed equidistribution between statistics on vincular pattern-avoiding permutations and inversion sequences.
345966.source_name: Zhicong Lin and Shishuo Fu, “On 120-avoiding inversion and ascent sequences”, arXiv:2003.11813 (2020).
345966.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.11813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

345971.title: Generalised Delta square conjecture, valley version
345971.statement:
Let $m,n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $h_m$ and $e_j$ be the complete homogeneous and elementary symmetric functions, and let $\Delta_f$ be the Delta operator. Let $\omega$ be the standard involution, $p_n$ the power-sum symmetric function, and $\mathsf{LSQ}(m,n)^{\bullet k}$ the set of labelled valley-decorated square paths of size $m+n$ with $m$ zero labels and $k$ decorations. For $\pi$ in this set, write $\mathsf{dinv}(\pi)$, $\mathsf{area}(\pi)$, and $x^\pi$ for its associated statistics and monomial weight.

**Generalised Delta square conjecture, valley version.**

$$
\frac{[n-k]_q}{[n]_q} \Delta_{h_m} \Delta_{e_{n-k}} \omega(p_n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathsf{LSQ}(m,n)^{\bullet k}} q^{\mathsf{dinv}(\pi)} t^{\mathsf{area}(\pi)} x^\pi.
$$

The paper reports computational evidence through $n=6$ and notes that this valley version differs from the rise version by replacing the $t$-analogue factor with a $q$-analogue factor. It remains open.
345971.source_name: Alessandro Iraci and Anna Vanden Wyngaerd, “A valley version of the Delta square conjecture”, arXiv:2003.12048 (2020).
345971.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12048

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2020).

346344.title: Loose-versus-non-exhaustive partition conjecture for metric graphs
346344.statement:
Fix a graph $\mathcal{G}$, a number $k\geq1$ and $p\in(0,\infty]$. Let $\mathcal{N}_p(\mathcal{P})$ denote the energy of a partition $\mathcal{P}$. A **non-exhaustive rigid $k$-partition** is a rigid partition whose parts do not exhaust $\mathcal{G}$, while an **exhaustive loose $k$-partition** is an exhaustive partition allowing the loose type of cuts considered in the paper. Define

$$
\mathcal{N}_{k,p}^{\mathrm{loose}}(\mathcal{G})=\inf\left\{\mathcal{N}_p(\mathcal{P}):\mathcal{P}\text{ is an exhaustive loose $k$-partition of }\mathcal{G}\right\}.
$$

**Loose-versus-non-exhaustive partition conjecture.** The infimum over non-exhaustive rigid $k$-partitions satisfies

$$
\inf\left\{\mathcal{N}_p(\mathcal{P}):\mathcal{P}\text{ is a non-exhaustive but rigid $k$-partition of }\mathcal{G}\right\}\geq\mathcal{N}_{k,p}^{\mathrm{loose}}(\mathcal{G}).
$$

The conjecture formalises the expectation that allowing loose exhaustive partitions is at least as effective as infimising over non-exhaustive rigid partitions. The paper motivates it through cutting and edge-lengthening surgery principles, but leaves the general statement for future work.
346344.source_name: James B. Kennedy, Pavel Kurasov, Corentin Léna and Delio Mugnolo, “A theory of spectral partitions of metric graphs”, arXiv:2005.01126 (2020).
346344.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.01126

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

346651.title: Alon–Yuster conjecture on orientations avoiding directed triangles
346651.statement:
Given a graph $G$ and an oriented graph $\vec H$, let $D(G,\vec H)$ be the number of orientations of $G$ containing no copy of $\vec H$, and define

$$
D(n,\vec H)=\max\{D(G,\vec H):G\text{ is an }n\text{-vertex graph}\}.
$$

Let $K^\circlearrowright_3$ denote the strongly connected orientation of a triangle. **Alon–Yuster's conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$,

$$
D(n,K^\circlearrowright_3)=\max\{2^{\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor},n!\}.
$$

The conjecture was posed by Alon and Yuster after they established the corresponding extremal behavior for sufficiently large $n$ and computed the values for small $n$. The paper confirms the conjecture and further shows that the balanced complete bipartite graph is the unique $n$-vertex extremal graph when the value is $2^{\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor}$, so the claim is solved.
346651.source_name: Pedro Araújo, Fábio Botler and Guilherme Oliveira Mota, “Counting graph orientations with no directed triangles”, arXiv:2005.13091 (2020).
346651.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.13091

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

346745.title: Parity congruences for hard-hexagon partition functions
346745.statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the partition function, with $p(m)=0$ for $m<0$. For a positive integer $k$, consider the two families of formal power series below, with $s\in\{2,4\}$ in the first and $s\in\{1,3\}$ in the second.

**Parity-coefficient conjecture.** For $s\in\{2,4\}$,

$$
\left(1+2\sum_{n=1}^{k}(-1)^nq^{2n^2}\right)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-q;q)_nq^{n(3n+s-1)/2}}{(q;q)_{2n+1}}-\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}(-1)^{n((s-1)n-1)/2}\left(q^{n(15n+3s-5)/2}+q^{(3n-s/2)(5n-3+s/2)/2}\right)
$$

has nonnegative coefficients if $k$ is even and nonpositive coefficients if $k$ is odd. For $s\in\{1,3\}$,

$$
\left(1+2\sum_{n=1}^{k}(-1)^nq^{2n^2}\right)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{q^{n(n+1)}}{(q;q)_{2n+(s-1)/2}}-\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}(-1)^{n(n+s)/2}q^{n(5n-s)/2}
$$

has nonnegative coefficients if $k$ is even and nonpositive coefficients if $k$ is odd.

The conjecture is motivated by substantial numerical evidence and would imply families of linear inequalities for the partition functions $R_s(n)$ and $R_s^*(n)$ arising from Baxter's hard-hexagon model. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.
346745.source_name: Mircea Merca, “q-Series congruences involving statistical mechanics partition functions in regime III and IV of Baxter's solution of the hard-hexagon model”, arXiv:2006.01691 (2020).
346745.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01691

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2020). “In Section , we will introduce new open problems involving the partition function $R_s(n)$, $s\in\{2,4\}$ and $R^*_s(n)$, $s\in\{1,3\}$.”

347853.title: Resonance-pole instability conjecture for inhomogeneous coupling
347853.statement:
Consider the modified system

$$
\begin{cases}
\partial_t u=d\partial_{xx}u+s\partial_xu+f(u)+\beta\sigma(x)v,\\
\partial_t v=-(\partial_{xx}+1)^2v+s\partial_xv+\mu v,
\end{cases}
\qquad t>0,\quad x\in\mathbb{R},
$$

where the coupling term $\beta v$ has been replaced by $\beta\sigma(x)v$, and suppose that the Fourier transform of $\sigma(x)$ has full support. **Resonance-pole instability conjecture.** For parameters in $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{abs}}$, the traveling wave $(Q_*(x),0)$ is pointwise unstable due to resonance poles accumulating on the unstable absolute spectrum $\Sigma_{\mathrm{abs}}$. This conjecture proposes a mechanism by which spatial inhomogeneity induces instability in a front that is stable in the corresponding homogeneous setting; the source presents numerical evidence and formulates the claim as a conjecture.
347853.source_name: Gregory Faye, Matt Holzer, Arnd Scheel and Lars Siemer, “Invasion into remnant instability: a case study of front dynamics”, arXiv:2009.02106 (2020).
347853.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02106

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2020).

348354.title: Forbidden-minor conjecture for non-even regular oriented matroids
348354.statement:
A **regular oriented matroid** is an oriented matroid whose underlying matroid is regular. For integers $m,n\geq 2$ with $m+n$ odd, let $\vec{K}_{m,n}$ denote the complete bipartite graph with its natural orientation, let $M^*(\vec{K}_{m,n})$ be its cographic oriented matroid, and let a $\mathsf{GB}$-minor be a minor obtained by the graphic-bond operations used in the paper. An oriented matroid is **non-even** when it is not even.

**Forbidden-minor conjecture.** A regular oriented matroid $M$ is non-even if and only if none of its $\mathsf{GB}$-minors is isomorphic to $M^*(\vec{K}_{m,n})$ for some $m,n\geq 2$ such that $m+n$ is odd.

The conjecture would identify the complete list of forbidden $\mathsf{GB}$-minors for non-even regular oriented matroids by combining the graphic and cographic cases. The paper reports computational evidence for the $10$-element regular matroid $R_{10}$; the general conjecture remains open, including the stated complexity problem for regular oriented matroids and the case of bond matroids.
348354.source_name: Karl Heuer, Raphael Steiner and Sebastian Wiederrecht, “Even Circuits in Oriented Matroids”, arXiv:2010.08988 (2020).
348354.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08988

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2020). “Apart from the obvious open problem of resolving the computational complexity of the even circuit problem () for regular oriented matroids in general, already resolving the case of bond matroids would be interesting.”

348761.title: Three symmetry conjectures for statistics on di-sk trees
348761.statement:
Let di-sk trees be the combinatorial objects considered in the paper, and let $\mathsf{omi}$, $\mathsf{riop}$, $\mathsf{rpop}$, $\mathsf{iop}$, and $\mathsf{pop}$ denote the statistics on them. For statistics $A_1,\ldots,A_k$, write $(A_1,\ldots,A_k)\sim(B_1,\ldots,B_k)$ when the corresponding statistic tuples are equidistributed over di-sk trees. The statistics $\mathsf{riop}$, $\mathsf{iop}$, $\mathsf{top}$, $\mathsf{pop}$, and $\mathsf{rpop}$ form an equidistributed quintuple.

**Three symmetry conjectures for di-sk trees.** Over di-sk trees, the following symmetries should hold:

$$
(\mathsf{omi},\mathsf{riop},\mathsf{rpop})\sim(\mathsf{omi},\mathsf{rpop},\mathsf{riop}),
$$

$$
(\mathsf{omi},\mathsf{iop},\mathsf{rpop})\sim(\mathsf{omi},\mathsf{rpop},\mathsf{iop}),
$$

$$
(\mathsf{riop},\mathsf{pop})\sim(\mathsf{pop},\mathsf{riop}).
$$

These conjectures propose the remaining symmetries suggested by computations after several related symmetries over di-sk trees had already been proved. The source gives no resolution of these three claims, so their status remains open.
348761.source_name: Shishuo Fu, Zhicong Lin and Yaling Wang, “A combinatorial bijection on di-sk trees”, arXiv:2011.11302 (2021).
348761.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11302

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

350614.title: Janson's height and width conjectures for simply generated trees
350614.statement:
Let ${\mathrm{w}}=(w_k,k \ge 0)$ be a weight sequence with $w_0>0$ and with $w_k>0$ for some $k \ge 2$. For $n \ge 0$ with $Z_n({\mathrm{w}})>0$, let ${\mathcal{T}}_n$ be a simply generated tree of size $n$ with weight sequence ${\mathrm{w}}$. The parameters $\nu$ and $\sigma^2$ are defined from the generating function of the weight sequence as in the setup above. **Janson's height and width conjectures.** Along integers $n$ such that $Z_n({\mathrm{w}})>0$, as $n\to\infty$, the following hold: (1) if $\nu=1$ and $\sigma^2=\infty$, then

$$
\frac{{\mathrm{ht}}({\mathcal{T}}_n)}{n^{1/2}}\to 0
$$

in probability; (2) if $\nu=1$ and $\sigma^2=\infty$, then

$$
\frac{{\mathrm{wid}}({\mathcal{T}}_n)}{n^{1/2}}\to\infty
$$

in probability; (3) if $\nu<1$, then

$$
\frac{{\mathrm{ht}}({\mathcal{T}}_n)}{n^{1/2}}\to 0
$$

in probability; and (4) if $\nu<1$, then

$$
\frac{{\mathrm{wid}}({\mathcal{T}}_n)}{n^{1/2}}\to\infty
$$

in probability. These assertions concern simply generated trees in the infinite-variance and condensation regimes, predicting subdiffusive height and superdiffusive width. The paper addresses these conjectures, so their resolution should be checked against the results stated elsewhere in the source.
350614.source_name: Louigi Addario-Berry, Anna Brandenberger, Jad Hamdan and Céline Kerriou, “Universal height and width bounds for random trees”, arXiv:2105.03195 (2022).
350614.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

352059.title: Component structure and vertex cardinalities of the digraph ${\cal D}^{*}_m$
352059.statement:
Let $m\geq 2$. The digraph ${\cal D}^{*}_m$ has components ${\cal A}^{*}_m$ and ${\cal B}^{*}_m$, where ${\cal B}^{*}_m$ consists of components ${\cal B}^{*(1)}_m,\ldots,{\cal B}^{*(\lfloor m/2\rfloor)}_m$ ordered by nonincreasing vertex cardinality. **Component-structure conjecture.** The digraph ${\cal D}^{*}_m$ has exactly $\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1$ components, all ${\cal B}^{*(k)}_m$ are bipartite, and

$$
|V({\cal B}^{*(k)}_m)|=
\begin{cases}
{m+1\choose (m+1)/2-k},&\text{if }m\text{ is odd},\\
2{m\choose m/2-k},&\text{if }m\text{ is even},
\end{cases}
$$

for $1\leq k\leq\lfloor m/2\rfloor$, while

$$
|V({\cal A}^{*}_m)|=
\begin{cases}
{m\choose (m-1)/2},&\text{if }m\text{ is odd},\\
{m\choose m/2},&\text{if }m\text{ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

Moreover, $v$ and $\overline v$ belong to the same component; if $v\in{\cal B}^{*(s)}_m$, then $\overline v$ is in the same class if and only if $m$ is odd. These properties were inferred from computational data and were stated for future study; no proof or resolution is supplied here.
352059.source_name: Jelena Djokić, Olga Bodroža-Pantić and Ksenija Doroslovački, “A spanning union of cycles in rectangular grid graphs, thick grid cylinders and Moebius strips”, arXiv:2109.12432 (2021).
352059.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

352200.title: Rademacher's conjecture on the extremal lattice for Landau's constant
352200.statement:
Let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{C}$ be discrete and $f_\Gamma \in \mathcal{U}$, where $\mathcal{U}$ is the class of universal covering maps of $\mathbb{D}$ onto $\mathbb{C} \backslash \Gamma$. Let $\ell(f_\Gamma)$ be the covering radius defined by

$$
\ell(f_\Gamma)=\sup\{r\in\mathbb{R}_+\mid D_r\subset f_\Gamma(\mathbb{D})\}.
$$

Then define $\mathcal{L}_\Gamma^{-1}=|f_\Gamma'(0)|/\ell(f_\Gamma)$. **Rademacher's conjecture.** The quantity

$$
\mathcal{L}_\Gamma^{-1}=\frac{|f_\Gamma'(0)|}{\ell(f_\Gamma)}
$$

is maximal for the hexagonal lattice.

This is the lattice formulation of the conjectural extremal description of Landau's constant. The supplied status evidence treats the conjecture as resolved, although the surrounding text in the source says that it is still open; this status should be checked against the cited literature.
352200.source_name: Laurent Bétermin, Markus Faulhuber and Stefan Steinerberger, “A variational principle for Gaussian lattice sums”, arXiv:2110.06008 (2021).
352200.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06008

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2021). “This is in accordance with the conjecture in , where also the value of $\mathcal{L}_{\Z^2}$ has been established numerically (see also ).”

352401.title: No broken diamond in hexagon conjecture for modified crystal operator paths
352401.statement:
Let $S_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the set of Kostant partitions under consideration, and let $k_i$ and $k_{i+1}$ be the positive integers associated with $\boldsymbol\alpha\in S_{\lambda,\mu}$ as in Definition~. Suppose that the modified crystal operators $\phi_i$ and $\phi_{i+1}$ are both non-zero on $\boldsymbol\alpha$. Define the paths

$$
E_i:=e_i^{k_{i+1}}e_{i+1}^{k_i+k_{i+1}}e_i^{k_i}(\boldsymbol\alpha),
$$

and

$$
E_{i+1}:=e_{i+1}^{k_i}e_i^{k_i+k_{i+1}}e_{i+1}^{k_{i+1}}(\boldsymbol\alpha).
$$

**No broken diamond in hexagon conjecture.** The paths $E_i$ and $E_{i+1}$ in the graph induced by the modified crystal operators do not contain any edges that give way to Stembridge Exception $\rm{BD}$. This conjecture is the condition used to establish the stated braid relations for the modified operators; the source reports that it is supported by computer testing, but gives no proof or resolution.
352401.source_name: Cédric Lecouvey, Cristian Lenart and Adam Schultze, “Towards a Combinatorial Model for q-weight Multiplicities of Simple Lie Algebras (Extended Abstract)”, arXiv:2110.15394 (2022).
352401.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15394

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

353017.title: The divisible-set union conjecture
353017.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. A set of points over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is $2^r$-divisible if every hyperplane meets it in a number of points congruent to its size modulo $2^r$. An $(r+1)$-space is a projective subspace of dimension $r+1$, and $[r+1]_2=(2^{r+1}-1)/(2-1)$ denotes its number of points.

**Divisible-set union conjecture.** There exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every $2^r$-divisible set of $f(r)\cdot [r+1]_2$ points over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is the disjoint union of $f(r)$ $(r+1)$-spaces and

$$
\lim_{r\to\infty} f(r)=\infty.
$$

This conjecture proposes arbitrarily large values of $r$ for which a sufficiently structured divisible set must decompose into disjoint spaces. The surrounding discussion gives related small-parameter results and computational evidence, but no resolution of this assertion is supplied.
353017.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.11763

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

355864.title: Conjecture on exceptional positive-indicator representations in even dimensions
355864.statement:
Let $J_n$ be the Hopf algebra considered in the paper. Fix an even integer $t$, write $n=mt$ for an integer $m\geq 2$, and consider irreducible representations of $J_n$ of dimension $t$ with indicator $+1$. Such a representation is induced from a permutation; say that the permutation **shares its orbit with an involution** when its orbit contains an involution.

**Even-dimensional exceptional-indicator conjecture.** The ratio of irreducible representations with indicator $+1$ induced from permutations that do not share their orbit with an involution to the total number of irreducible representations of dimension $t$ with indicator $+1$ converges to $0$ as $m\to\infty$.

The conjecture formalizes the computational observation that most positive-indicator representations in even dimension arise from orbits containing an involution. The paper does not provide a formula for counting the exceptional representations, so the claim remains open.
355864.source_name: Kayla Orlinsky, “An Indicator Formula for the Hopf Algebra k^S_n-1\#kC_n”, arXiv:2208.12714 (2022).
355864.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12714

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).
